name: Giuseppe Sabetta
topic: Support for defining security requirements using LLM and RAG
description: Development and evaluation of a system based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Large Language Models (LLM) to automate the generation and formalization of traceable security requirements starting from a natural language Problem Statement, integrating OWASP guidelines and cheat sheets[cite: 54, 233, 269].

name: Giovanni Scorziello
topic: Prompt Syntax Tree: A Formal Representation for the Analysis and Automatic Decompositions of LLM Prompts
description: Proposal and formalization of the Prompt Syntax Tree (PST), a hierarchical data structure inspired by compiler theory (AST) to decompose prompts into addressable semantic units[cite: 1201, 1257]. The work includes the curation of an annotated dataset and the fine-tuning of a Llama-3-8B language model for automatic prompt parsing[cite: 1204, 1263].

name: Aniello Giamundo
topic: Impact of Generative AI on Code Structural Quality: A Pre and Post Adoption Longitudinal Empirical Study on Open Source Repositories
description: An empirical, longitudinal study on 90 open-source repositories to analyze the impact of Generative AI (GenAI) tool adoption on code structural quality. By leveraging SonarQube and GitPython metrics in pre/post-adoption windows defined via Self-Admitted GenAI Usage (SAGU), the study highlights statistically significant increases in cyclomatic complexity, cognitive complexity, technical debt, and code smells, with no significant changes to code churn and duplication.

name: Salvatore Amoroso
topic: Semantic Docstring Perturbations and Security of LLM-Generated Code: An Analysis under Dual-Oracle Evaluation
description: A black-box study of whether semantic perturbations of docstrings, which preserve functional intent, induce a code-specialized open LLM to generate functionally correct but insecure code. Three attack techniques with decreasing explicitness (ExampleBased, InverseComment, SemanticPriming) are evaluated with the CWEval dual runtime oracle on 119 tasks, 31 CWE categories and 5 languages. InverseComment makes 34.78% of baseline-secure tasks insecure, ExampleBased 21.74% and SemanticPriming only 2.17%, suggesting that attack effectiveness depends on how directly the perturbation imposes the weakness on the model.
